clue.text: Return to cut crop up and divide

indicators.note: return to the start of the word, so the word for cut is read backwards

parts.note: to lop is to cut
to crop up is to arise

explanation.surface: A farmer goes back to harvesting a crop that has sprung up, then splits it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crop up' looks like farming, but together the words mean arise; 'Return to' covers only the word for cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To polarise opinion is to split it into opposing camps, a synonym for divide.

clue.text: Report that's exciting discussion

parts.note: a report is a bang, which can be written pow
wow is an exclamation meaning that's exciting

explanation.surface: A news report describes a stimulating debate.
explanation.definitionFit: A powwow is an informal meeting or conference for discussion.

clue.text: A cash register turned up containing old book

indicators.note: containing means holding the abbreviation for old inside
in a down entry, turned up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a till is a cash register

explanation.surface: Inside an upturned shop till lies an antique volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' makes LLITA from A TILL; 'containing' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lolita is Nabokov's 1955 novel, so it is a book.

clue.text: Protester gets soldiers to join clan rising

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
to fuse is to join

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word reads upwards

parts.note: kin are one's clan or family

explanation.surface: A dissident enlists troops to join a tribal revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusenik was a Soviet Jew refused emigration, and by extension anyone who refuses to comply in protest.

clue.text: Rum on vessel — queen's pinched a tiny bit

indicators.note: pinched means squeezed between, so the queen sits between the rum word and the vessel

parts.note: rum means odd, strange
an ark is a vessel, as Noah's was
QU is an abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A queen helps herself to rum aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' is not the drink but the old British adjective for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A strange quark is one of the elementary particles, a tiny subatomic bit of matter.

clue.text: One punching jaw, senselessly

definitions.meaning: to jaw is to talk, and talking senselessly is to ...

explanation.definitionFit: A jabber is literally one who jabs; to jabber is to chatter without sense, which is jawing.

clue.text: Swimming in the sea's what you regularly take up

indicators.note: take up in a down clue means the letters are read upwards
regularly means every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Swimming in the sea is something you ought to take up regularly.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of 'the sea's what' are HSAWA; 'take up' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: Awash means flooded or covered with water, as if swimming in it.

clue.text: In one's good books

parts.note: the idiom means in favour, but read literally it means found in the Good Book, scripture

explanation.definitionFit: Biblical means appearing in or relating to the Bible, the Good Book.

clue.text: Was persistent successor to do better? About right

parts.note: in sol-fa, re comes after do

indicators.note: about means going around, so the word for better wraps the R

parts.note: a patient who is better is cured

explanation.surface: Someone who follows wonders how to improve and asks about rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' is the sol-fa note, not a verb: its successor in the scale is RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that recurred kept coming back, so it was persistent.

clue.text: Ballistic launch that moves fast over forest

parts.note: going ballistic is going wild with fury
to fire a missile is to launch it

explanation.surface: A missile launch races across woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: A wildfire is a blaze in open country that spreads rapidly through trees and scrub.

clue.text: In the small hours, bishop in charge regularly stressed

parts.note: one in the morning, written 1 AM with the numeral as I, is in the small hours
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop on duty overnight finds himself under regular strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The small hours' gives 1 AM, with the figure one read as the letter I. 'regularly' belongs to the definition; it is not telling you to take alternate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Iambic verse has a regular beat of unstressed then stressed syllables, so it is regularly stressed.

clue.text: Sweet bachelor with pure spirit

parts.note: utter means complete, pure
Scotch whisky is a spirit

explanation.surface: An unmarried man drinks neat whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterscotch is a hard toffee-like confection, a type of sweet.

clue.text: Polar explorer has extra-large clothing tucked away

indicators.note: clothing something wraps it, so the size label goes around the eating word

parts.note: OS is outsize, the label for extra-large clothes
to tuck away food is to eat it, so ATE

explanation.surface: An Antarctic explorer has his big clothes packed away.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Lawrence Oates died on Scott's 1912 South Pole expedition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawrence Oates was a member of Scott's doomed expedition to the South Pole.

clue.text: Love attention, it's said, being more unruly

indicators.note: it's said tells us the result is what the words sound like when spoken

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, nought; to lend an ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: Craving affection and attention makes a child behave worse.
explanation.definitionFit: Naughtier means more badly behaved, a comparative synonym for more unruly.

clue.text: Fashionable green beret woven without a missing cord

parts.note: IN means in fashion
vert is green in heraldry

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the shuffled beret goes around the a
woven suggests the letters of beret are worked into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A trendy green beret is knitted, but the drawstring has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woven' makes EBRTE from BERET, and 'without' puts it outside A, giving EBRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An invertebrate has no backbone, so it is an animal lacking a spinal cord.

clue.text: Head brought up exam books for one enjoying best courses

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means the word is read upwards

parts.note: nob is slang for head
a viva is an oral exam
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A headmaster revisits exam papers for a gifted student.
explanation.definitionFit: A bon vivant enjoys good food and drink, so fine courses at dinner suit him.

clue.text: Shorter plug fitted with spanner

indicators.note: fitted with means the plug word has the spanner placed inside

parts.note: an ad plugs a product
a bridge spans a river

explanation.surface: An electrical plug is attached with a wrench.
explanation.definitionFit: An abridged text has been cut down, so it is shorter.

clue.text: Car that's dropping off passengers

parts.note: not a taxi setting people down but a railway carriage where travellers nod off to sleep

explanation.definitionFit: A wagon-lit is a sleeping car on a continental European train.

clue.text: Maybe cordial knight captured by dirty scoundrels

parts.note: black means filthy, dirty

indicators.note: captured by means held inside the rogues' words

parts.note: a cur and a rat are both scoundrels
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight is taken prisoner by a gang of filthy rogues.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackcurrant is a common flavour of fruit cordial, so cordial is an example, hence the maybe.

clue.text: Awful pun by one monstrous Australian

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: I is the roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A terrible joke told by a monster from Down Under.
explanation.definitionFit: The bunyip is a monster of Aboriginal Australian folklore said to lurk in swamps.

clue.text: Hum a number in school

indicators.note: in means the number goes inside the school abbreviation

parts.note: ten is a number

explanation.surface: A school choir hums a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hum' is not singing but British slang for a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Hum is informal British for an unpleasant smell, a synonym for stench.

clue.text: Eroticism in pieces of equal size

indicators.note: in pieces says the word is broken up and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: Sensuality is shown in equal portions.
explanation.definitionFit: Isometric means having equal dimensions or measurements.

clue.text: Inspiring female runs in fast?

indicators.note: in places the runs abbreviation inside the fasting phrase

parts.note: to fast is to eat nothing, read as eat followed by O for zero
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A motivating woman runs during a period of fasting.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark warns that 'fast' must be read playfully as EAT O, eat nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is one of the nine Muses, who inspire artists, so she is an inspiring female.

clue.text: Northern folk's short stay in Paris hotel?

parts.note: a brief hotel booking in France might read one night, written as the numeral one and the French word for night
nuit is French for night, the second half of the booking

explanation.surface: Arctic people take a brief break in a French hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsy: a one-night booking in Paris is '1 nuit', with I standing for the figure one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inuit are indigenous peoples of the Arctic regions of Canada, Greenland and Alaska.

clue.text: Means to follow female in Irish city

indicators.note: to follow places the word for means after the word for female

parts.note: a gal is a woman
a way is a means of doing something

explanation.surface: A method for a woman to pursue in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: GALWAY is a city on the west coast of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Galway is a city in the west of Ireland, county town of County Galway.

clue.text: Be reasonable, and yet so absurd

indicators.note: absurd suggests the letters of and yet so are scrambled into nonsense

explanation.surface: A reply that both accepts and dismisses an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady on is an exclamation urging someone to calm down and be moderate.

clue.text: Firm has over the counter stuff to make millions

indicators.note: to stuff is to pack inside, so the counter abbreviation goes into the other pieces

parts.note: to do something is to make it
OTC is the abbreviation for over the counter
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A company plans to sell over-the-counter goods and get rich.
explanation.definitionFit: A dotcom is an internet-based company, a kind of firm.

clue.text: Cold shed with unknown source of power leading to a hot cheek

indicators.note: leading to means the earlier pieces come before the rest

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
a hut is a shed
Z is an algebraic unknown

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: A chilly shed with a mystery power supply leads to a hot face.
explanation.definitionFit: Chutzpah is audacious nerve, a near synonym for cheek in the sense of impudence.
